name: Andaz San Diego
positioning: Boutique downtown hotel in San Diego's Gaslamp District, in a historic building with the Gaslamp Quarter's largest rooftop
best_for: Travelers who want a lively downtown base surrounded by nightlife and dining
Guests who want rooftop pool days with cabanas and skyline views

facts.text: The boutique hotel is in San Diego's Gaslamp District, downtown.
The hotel's historic building opened in 1913 for the World's Fair celebrating the Panama Canal.
Condé Nast Traveler notes the hotel was originally the Ivy Hotel.
The hotel is a half mile from Petco Park.
The hotel is surrounded by vibrant nightlife, upscale dining and popular attractions.
The Rooftop by STK is the hotel's open-air rooftop restaurant.
STK Steakhouse has a central lounge with leather banquettes, theatrical lighting and a DJ.
Registered guests can join a complimentary beer and wine tasting in the lobby each evening.
The hotel welcomes dogs, with dog beds, Andaz bowls and a treat at the front desk.
The hotel has a fitness center.

highlights.text: The hotel has the Gaslamp Quarter's largest rooftop, with a restaurant, bar and pool.
The Andaz Cabana Suite has access to a private poolside cabana via a spiral staircase.
At the rooftop pool, guests can reserve a day pass, cabana or daybed with skyline views.
The Andaz Sweet Suite is a top-floor suite with city views, an eight-person dining table and two bathrooms.

considerations.text: Parking at the hotel is by valet.
San Diego International Airport is 2.5 miles from the hotel.
WhataHotel notes an urban setting with potential street noise.
